beats.line: My Gym Jarvis checked twenty-three sets, and called stop on a good one.
I spent months of weekends on Gym Jarvis, so let's open my Workout Analyser.
After over 200 papers and tools, I realized counting reps is easy, but judging one is hard.
So I built one pose tool and two agents.
It tracks my joints, and rep maths turns each rep into a wave.
A taller wave means I moved further, so cut-short reps look shorter.
And like a trainer, it compares each wave with my own best.
The first agent is the judge, which reads my numbers.
The second agent is the coach, a second opinion that isn't allowed the numbers.
And one guardrail before any AI: if the code can't see the joint, it won't judge.
Then I ran every set, and almost none got a stop.
Except this one, where the judge said stop and the coach said good.
I had only turned towards the camera, like the research warned.
So now, stop needs both agents to agree, or I check the footage.
And only one stop survived, my reverse crunch.
And it was right: my worst rep was under half my best.
Send this to a friend who swears every rep is full.
Next up: Salesforce is reportedly letting people go, but hiring people with AI experience.
How can you be that one? Follow along to know.

Beat 11: was 'Then I ran every set, and most were continue or hold.' Now 'Then I ran every set, and almost none got a stop.' It no longer uses 'continue' or 'hold' before they are introduced, and it sets up 'Except this one' in beat 12. It matches facts.md: 1 final STOP and 1 CHECK FOOTAGE out of 23, with the dashboard carrying the exact counts.
Beat 15 split into beats 15 and 16 exactly as given. 'Under half my best' matches facts.md: worst rep 53 degrees against best rep 122 degrees, and half of 122 is 61.
Beat 17 inserted before the Salesforce beat exactly as given: 'Send this to a friend who swears every rep is full.'
Beats 1, 3-10 and 12-14 are word for word. The last two lines (now beats 18 and 19) are word for word. No semicolons. The script is now 19 beats.
